title: Descending search reaches the first positive test
statement: Let a register machine have $m$ registers, states in a type $\Lambda$, and an oracle on $d$ Boolean-string inputs. Fix a register $r$, a decidable predicate $P$ on the natural numbers, states $\mathrm{test},\mathrm{yes},\mathrm{dec}\in\Lambda$, a bound $B$, and a register valuation $v$ with every register at most $B$. Assume that from state $\mathrm{test}$, with register $r$ set to any $c'$, one step leaves the registers unchanged and goes to $\mathrm{yes}$ if $P(c')$ holds and to $\mathrm{dec}$ otherwise; also assume every configuration at state $\mathrm{test}$ with no result satisfies the machine's precondition, and that state $\mathrm{dec}$ decrements register $r$ and returns to $\mathrm{test}$. For any $c$ satisfying $P(c)$, every $c_0$ with $c<c_0\le B$ and with no $c'$ strictly between $c$ and $c_0$ satisfying $P(c')$, the machine can reach the configuration at state $\mathrm{yes}$ with register valuation $v$ updated to $c$ at $r$ and no result, starting from state $\mathrm{dec}$ with that register set to $c_0$ and no result; throughout this run, every visited configuration before the final one satisfies the guard requiring the precondition and all registers to be at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: A register machine $A$ and oracle on $d$ Boolean strings
A natural-number bound $B$ and register valuation $v$
Every register value in $v$ is at most $B$
The specified one-step behavior from $\mathrm{test}$ for every $c'$
Every no-result configuration at $\mathrm{test}$ satisfies the precondition
State $\mathrm{dec}$ decrements register $r$ and returns to $\mathrm{test}$
